file.content:
name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    (via `release:publish` → scripts/release/publish-npm.ts, the npm CLI) and cuts a GitHub release per
#    package from the script's `New tag:` stdout.
#
# Token-free: publishing uses npm OIDC "trusted publishing" (`id-token: write` + `npm publish`), not an
# `NPM_TOKEN`. Requires (one-time): repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow
# GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR), and a
# trusted publisher for EACH published package on npmjs.com (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
# GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow `release.yml`). A package with no trusted
# publisher 404s on publish; the script logs it and continues, so the rest still ship.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Two things OIDC "trusted publishing" needs, done after the toolchain is fully set up:
      #  - npm ≥ 11.5.1 (Node 22 bundles an older npm that doesn't know the OIDC flow).
      #  - No `_authToken` line in the npmrc. setup-node's `registry-url` always writes
      #    `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`; with the token unset, npm treats that
      #    empty entry as configured auth and fails ENEEDAUTH instead of falling back to OIDC
      #    (actions/setup-node#1551). Strip it so npm does the token exchange.
      - name: Prepare npm for OIDC publishing
        run: |
          npm install -g npm@latest
          npmrc="${NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG:-$HOME/.npmrc}"
          if [ -f "$npmrc" ]; then sed -i '/_authToken/d' "$npmrc"; fi
          echo "using npm $(npm --version)"

      # The changesets action takes one of two paths per run: with pending changesets it opens/updates the
      # Version PR (just `changeset version` — no dist needed); with none it publishes. Only the publish
      # path needs a build, so gate it — otherwise every feature merge (which carries a changeset) rebuilds
      # here even though CI already built the same commit. Mirrors the action's own version-vs-publish call.
      - name: Determine release mode
        id: mode
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -n "$(find .changeset -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' ! -name 'README.md' -print -quit)" ]; then
            echo "will_publish=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Pending changesets → Version PR path; skipping build."
          else
            echo "will_publish=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No changesets → publish path; building."
          fi

      # Build so the publish step ships real dist/. prepublishOnly was removed repo-wide (#23), so no
      # package re-invokes a nested `vp` at pack time.
      - name: Build all packages
        if: steps.mode.outputs.will_publish == 'true'
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          # Publish is invoked as plain `node`, NOT `vp run`: the `vp run` launcher scrubs the
          # `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL/TOKEN` env vars (and `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`) from the task
          # subprocess, so npm logged "oidc Skipped because incorrect permissions for id-token" and fell
          # back to ENEEDAUTH. Running node directly under the action's env lets npm see the OIDC token
          # request vars and do the trusted-publishing exchange.
          publish: node scripts/release/publish-npm.ts
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
          # The publish script owns tags + GitHub releases (via `gh release create`), so the action must
          # not also try (its `git push origin <tag>` needs a local tag + persisted credentials we don't
          # provide). See scripts/release/publish-npm.ts.
          createGithubReleases: false
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"

name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    (via `release:publish` → scripts/release/publish-npm.ts, the npm CLI) and cuts a GitHub release per
#    package from the script's `New tag:` stdout.
#
# Token-free: publishing uses npm OIDC "trusted publishing" (`id-token: write` + `npm publish`), not an
# `NPM_TOKEN`. Requires (one-time): repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow
# GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR), and a
# trusted publisher for EACH published package on npmjs.com (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
# GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow `release.yml`). A package with no trusted
# publisher 404s on publish; the script logs it and continues, so the rest still ship.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Two things OIDC "trusted publishing" needs, done after the toolchain is fully set up:
      #  - npm ≥ 11.5.1 (Node 22 bundles an older npm that doesn't know the OIDC flow).
      #  - No `_authToken` line in the npmrc. setup-node's `registry-url` always writes
      #    `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`; with the token unset, npm treats that
      #    empty entry as configured auth and fails ENEEDAUTH instead of falling back to OIDC
      #    (actions/setup-node#1551). Strip it so npm does the token exchange.
      - name: Prepare npm for OIDC publishing
        run: |
          npm install -g npm@latest
          npmrc="${NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG:-$HOME/.npmrc}"
          if [ -f "$npmrc" ]; then sed -i '/_authToken/d' "$npmrc"; fi
          echo "using npm $(npm --version)"

      # The changesets action takes one of two paths per run: with pending changesets it opens/updates the
      # Version PR (just `changeset version` — no dist needed); with none it publishes. Only the publish
      # path needs a build, so gate it — otherwise every feature merge (which carries a changeset) rebuilds
      # here even though CI already built the same commit. Mirrors the action's own version-vs-publish call.
      - name: Determine release mode
        id: mode
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -n "$(find .changeset -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' ! -name 'README.md' -print -quit)" ]; then
            echo "will_publish=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Pending changesets → Version PR path; skipping build."
          else
            echo "will_publish=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No changesets → publish path; building."
          fi

      # Build so the publish step ships real dist/. prepublishOnly was removed repo-wide (#23), so no
      # package re-invokes a nested `vp` at pack time.
      - name: Build all packages
        if: steps.mode.outputs.will_publish == 'true'
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          # Publish is invoked as plain `node`, NOT `vp run`: the `vp run` launcher scrubs the
          # `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL/TOKEN` env vars (and `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`) from the task
          # subprocess, so npm logged "oidc Skipped because incorrect permissions for id-token" and fell
          # back to ENEEDAUTH. Running node directly under the action's env lets npm see the OIDC token
          # request vars and do the trusted-publishing exchange.
          publish: node scripts/release/publish-npm.ts
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
          # The publish script owns tags + GitHub releases (via `gh release create`), so the action must
          # not also try (its `git push origin <tag>` needs a local tag + persisted credentials we don't
          # provide). See scripts/release/publish-npm.ts.
          createGithubReleases: false
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"

content.text:
Done. Here's what happened and what I changed.

## What went wrong

You did wire in a PAT — commit `54b848b` ("ci: open the changesets Version PR with a fine-grained PAT"). But the OIDC publishing migration right after it (PR #24, `3efb6d0`) regenerated `release.yml` from the pre-PAT template and silently dropped `RELEASE_PAT`, reverting checkout to `persist-credentials: false` and the changesets env back to `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`.

That's the whole cause. PRs opened by the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` never trigger downstream workflows (GitHub's anti-recursion rule), so the "Version Packages" PR's release and CI checks park in `action_required` waiting for a manual click.

## The fix

Restored the PAT wiring in [release.yml](.github/workflows/release.yml):
- **Checkout** uses `token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}` so the version branch push and PR are authored by a real user.
- **Changesets action env** `GITHUB_TOKEN` points at `RELEASE_PAT`, which also flows to the publish script's `gh release create` (needs Contents: write).
- Updated the header comment to document `RELEASE_PAT` alongside the OIDC requirements, and to make clear the PAT is git/PR auth only — npm publishing stays OIDC/token-free.

No change needed in `ci.yml`; it already triggers on `pull_request`, and it'll run automatically once the PR is PAT-authored.

## One thing to verify on your end

The `RELEASE_PAT` secret must still exist in repo settings (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions), fine-grained, scoped to this repo, with **Contents: read/write** and **Pull requests: read/write**. It predates the OIDC churn, so it's probably still there — but if it was removed or expired, this workflow will fail at checkout. Worth a quick glance before the next release run.

Want me to commit this on the current `chore/package-metadata` branch, or should it go on its own `ci/` branch to match your PR pattern?

name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    (via `release:publish` → scripts/release/publish-npm.ts, the npm CLI) and cuts a GitHub release per
#    package from the script's `New tag:` stdout.
#
# Token-free npm auth: publishing uses npm OIDC "trusted publishing" (`id-token: write` + `npm publish`),
# not an `NPM_TOKEN`. Requires (one-time):
#  - repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow GitHub Actions to create and
#    approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR);
#  - a trusted publisher for EACH published package on npmjs.com (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
#    GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow `release.yml`). A package with no trusted
#    publisher 404s on publish; the script logs it and continues, so the rest still ship;
#  - a `RELEASE_PAT` secret: a fine-grained personal access token scoped to this repo with Contents:
#    read/write + Pull requests: read/write. The Version PR is opened (and its branch pushed) with this
#    token so CI runs on it automatically. PRs authored by the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN don't trigger
#    workflows — their checks sit in `action_required` and need a manual click. The PAT is git/PR auth
#    only; it has nothing to do with npm publishing, which stays OIDC/token-free.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Check out with the fine-grained PAT so the Version PR (and its branch push) is authored by a
          # real user, not the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN — that's what lets CI run on the PR automatically
          # instead of parking its checks in `action_required`.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Two things OIDC "trusted publishing" needs, done after the toolchain is fully set up:
      #  - npm ≥ 11.5.1 (Node 22 bundles an older npm that doesn't know the OIDC flow).
      #  - No `_authToken` line in the npmrc. setup-node's `registry-url` always writes
      #    `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`; with the token unset, npm treats that
      #    empty entry as configured auth and fails ENEEDAUTH instead of falling back to OIDC
      #    (actions/setup-node#1551). Strip it so npm does the token exchange.
      - name: Prepare npm for OIDC publishing
        run: |
          npm install -g npm@latest
          npmrc="${NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG:-$HOME/.npmrc}"
          if [ -f "$npmrc" ]; then sed -i '/_authToken/d' "$npmrc"; fi
          echo "using npm $(npm --version)"

      # The changesets action takes one of two paths per run: with pending changesets it opens/updates the
      # Version PR (just `changeset version` — no dist needed); with none it publishes. Only the publish
      # path needs a build, so gate it — otherwise every feature merge (which carries a changeset) rebuilds
      # here even though CI already built the same commit. Mirrors the action's own version-vs-publish call.
      - name: Determine release mode
        id: mode
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -n "$(find .changeset -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' ! -name 'README.md' -print -quit)" ]; then
            echo "will_publish=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Pending changesets → Version PR path; skipping build."
          else
            echo "will_publish=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No changesets → publish path; building."
          fi

      # Build so the publish step ships real dist/. prepublishOnly was removed repo-wide (#23), so no
      # package re-invokes a nested `vp` at pack time.
      - name: Build all packages
        if: steps.mode.outputs.will_publish == 'true'
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          # Publish is invoked as plain `node`, NOT `vp run`: the `vp run` launcher scrubs the
          # `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL/TOKEN` env vars (and `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`) from the task
          # subprocess, so npm logged "oidc Skipped because incorrect permissions for id-token" and fell
          # back to ENEEDAUTH. Running node directly under the action's env lets npm see the OIDC token
          # request vars and do the trusted-publishing exchange.
          publish: node scripts/release/publish-npm.ts
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
          # The publish script owns tags + GitHub releases (via `gh release create`), so the action must
          # not also try (its `git push origin <tag>` needs a local tag + persisted credentials we don't
          # provide). See scripts/release/publish-npm.ts.
          createGithubReleases: false
        env:
          # RELEASE_PAT (not the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN): the action uses it to push the version branch +
          # open the PR as a real user (so CI triggers), and the publish script's `gh release create`
          # inherits it for cutting releases (Contents: write). npm auth is separate (OIDC), so no token
          # here touches publishing.
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"

content.text:
Opened [PR #36](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/36). Here's the full picture.

## What actually happened

The `RELEASE_PAT` secret **never existed**. `gh secret list` shows only `NPM_TOKEN`. Commit `54b848b` back in July referenced `secrets.RELEASE_PAT`, the OIDC migration removed that reference before anyone hit the code path, and my PR #35 re-added it as a *hard requirement*. An empty `token:` makes `actions/checkout` fail outright — so main went red and publishing was blocked.

## What PR #36 does

- Falls back to the built-in token when `RELEASE_PAT` is empty, so main goes green and releases publish again.
- Adds a `::warning::` in the release log whenever the PAT is missing, so the fallback isn't silent.
- The moment you add the secret, auto-CI on the Version PR activates — no further workflow edit.

Merge #36 to unblock main.

## The one thing only you can do

To actually get CI running on the Version PR (the original goal), create the secret. Generate a fine-grained PAT at GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Fine-grained tokens: scope it to `thedannywahl/pantoken`, with **Contents: read/write** and **Pull requests: read/write**. Then either add it via the repo UI, or:

```bash
gh secret set RELEASE_PAT --repo thedannywahl/pantoken
```

Note the PAT will expire (fine-grained tokens max out at ~1 year) — when it does, the release log's warning is your signal to rotate it.

Want me to close PR #35 since #36 supersedes it?

The RELEASE_PAT token needs specific permissions to handle the workflow steps: it requires **Contents: read/write** for the checkout action to push the version branch and for creating GitHub releases, and **Pull requests: read/write** for the changesets action to open and update the Version Packages PR.

Metadata: read is automatically included as mandatory for fine-grained PATs. Workflows permission isn't needed since the version branch only modifies package.json, CHANGELOG.md, and changeset files—not workflow files. The PR authored by the PAT will naturally trigger CI as a side effect, and the repo setting about GitHub Actions creating PRs only applies to GITHUB_TOKEN, not the PAT.

content.text:
A fine-grained PAT scoped to **only `thedannywahl/pantoken`**, with these repository permissions:

| Permission | Level | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Contents** | Read and write | Push the version branch, and let the publish script's `gh release create` cut tags + releases |
| **Pull requests** | Read and write | Open and update the "Version Packages" PR |
| **Metadata** | Read | Mandatory — GitHub auto-selects it whenever any other permission is set |

That's the whole list. Notable things it does **not** need:

- **Workflows** — the version branch push only touches `package.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `.changeset/*.md`. It never edits files under `.github/workflows/`, so the special Workflows scope isn't required. (If you ever grant it, fine, but it's unnecessary surface.)
- **Actions, Administration, or any org-level scope** — none of it is touched.

The CI-triggering behavior isn't a permission — it's a side effect of the PR being authored by a real user (the token owner) instead of `github-actions[bot]`. Contents + Pull requests write is exactly what makes that happen.

One caveat: the token inherits *your* access, so releases and the Version PR will show as authored by your account. If you'd rather not tie the automation to a personal identity long-term, a GitHub App installation token is the alternative — more setup, but not owned by one person. For now the PAT is the simpler path and matches what the workflow already expects.

### The Version PR needs a PAT to trigger CI — and an unset secret hard-fails checkout

**Symptom** — The changesets "Version Packages" PR opened, but its CI and release checks sat in
`action_required` and never ran. Wiring a PAT reference into the release workflow to fix that turned
main red instead: `actions/checkout` failed with `Input required and not supplied: token`.

the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` (anti-recursion), so a Version PR opened by the changesets action never
kicks off CI. (2) `actions/checkout`'s `token:` input, given the empty string a not-yet-created
`secrets.*` resolves to, errors out rather than falling back — so referencing a missing secret breaks
the whole workflow, including the publish path.

read/write) on both the checkout `token:` and the changesets action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` env, so the PR
comes from a real user and CI runs automatically. Reference the secret defensively —
`${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT || github.token }}` — so an absent or expired PAT degrades to the built-in
token instead of hard-failing, and emit a `::warning::` when it's missing. The PAT is git/PR auth only;
npm publishing stays OIDC/token-free (`id-token: write` + trusted publishers). Fine-grained PATs expire
(≤ 1 year); the "RELEASE_PAT missing" warning in the release log is the rotation cue.

The solution is to create an aggregation job — something like `ci-ok` or `all-checks-pass` — that depends on all the other jobs and acts as a single gate for the merge.

All green — the merge is clean, no revert needed. Now to your ask.

Here's the landscape. Two workflows post PR checks, and the trap is the **conditional** jobs:

| Workflow | Jobs | Conditional (skipped on some PRs) |
|---|---|---|
| `ci.yml` | build, typecheck, test, lint, publint, attw, repository, commitlint, docs-changes, docs | `docs` (only if docs changed), `commitlint` (PR-only) |
| `changeset-check.yml` | detect-release-impact, require-changeset, docs-and-internal-only | `require-changeset` / `docs-and-internal-only` (mutually exclusive by release impact) |

The naive fix — list every check as "required" in branch protection — **breaks** on exactly those conditional jobs: a required check that gets skipped is never reported, so GitHub parks the PR at "Expected — waiting for status" forever. And the required list would need editing every time a job is added or renamed.

## Recommended approach: one gate job per workflow

Add a `ci-gate` job to `ci.yml` and a `changeset-gate` job to `changeset-check.yml`. Each `needs:` every other job in its workflow, runs with `if: always()`, and fails only if a dependency actually **failed or was cancelled** — treating *skipped* as fine. Then branch protection requires just those two gate checks.

Why this answers "regardless of which workflow":
- Each workflow carries its own gate; requiring both means a PR merges only when *both* workflows are fully resolved and green.
- The required-checks list is **two stable names** that never change as jobs come and go.
- Conditional/skipped jobs no longer block.
- `gh pr merge --auto` then genuinely waits, because there's a required check that stays pending until everything resolves.

The one alternative — requiring each check individually — I'd reject for the skip-trap and maintenance churn above.

This is two parts: a **workflow code change** (safe, reviewable) and a **branch-protection change** (admin, and consequential — a bad config blocks all merges). Order matters: land the gate jobs on main first, *then* require them, so no PR blocks waiting on a check that doesn't exist yet.

repository:
    # Pure manifest read — no build needed. Catches a missing repository.url (which breaks npm OIDC
    # provenance) on the PR instead of at release.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Check repository metadata
        run: vp run gate:repository

  commitlint:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Lint PR commit messages
        run: vp exec commitlint --from "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}" --to "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" --verbose

  # Detect docs-relevant changes so PRs only pay for the docs build when the site could change. Runs on
  # both events (never skipped) so the `docs` job's `needs` is always satisfied.
  docs-changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      docs: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Detect docs-relevant changes
        id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@v4
        with:
          filters: |
            docs:
              - 'docs/**'
              - 'packages/**'
              - 'formats/**'
              - 'platforms/**'
              - 'renderers/**'
              - 'plugins/**'
              - 'design/**'
              - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
              - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'

  # Build the site as part of CI, so:
  #  - PRs get the exact deploy command run — a broken build OR a stale translation cache
  #    (check-locale-drift) blocks the PR instead of only surfacing in the post-merge Deploy docs run.
  #  - main pushes upload the built site as `docs-site`, which the Deploy docs workflow publishes
  #    directly (no rebuild).
  # Gated on docs-relevant changes with the same path set the Deploy docs `changes` job uses, so the
  # artifact is uploaded exactly when a deploy will look for it.
  docs:
    needs: [build, docs-changes]
    if: needs.docs-changes.outputs.docs == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Build docs (locale parity + drift + VitePress build)
        run: vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build
        env:
          DOCS_BASE: /
          DOCS_HOSTNAME: https://pantoken.iywahl.com/
      # On main, hand the built site to the Deploy docs workflow (workflow_run) so it publishes without
      # rebuilding. The CNAME is baked in here so the downloaded artifact is deploy-ready as-is.
      - name: Add custom domain file
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: echo "pantoken.iywahl.com" > docs/.vitepress/dist/CNAME
      - name: Upload built docs site
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: docs-site
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist
          retention-days: 1

require-changeset:
    needs: detect-release-impact
    if: needs.detect-release-impact.outputs.release_impact == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      # A pull_request checkout lands in detached HEAD with no local `main`, so `changeset status`
      # can't find where HEAD diverged from the base branch. Materialize it as a local ref.
      - name: Make base branch available for changeset diff
        run: git fetch --no-tags origin +refs/heads/${{ github.base_ref }}:refs/heads/${{ github.base_ref }}

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # `release:coverage` is the gate: it fails when a changed publishable package has no pending
      # changeset bumping it. It supersedes a bare `changeset status` — it ignores private packages and
      # dev-only package.json changes (scripts/devDependencies), which `changeset status` would wrongly
      # flag. Skipped on the changesets bot's "Version Packages" PR (it bumps package.json and deletes
      # the changesets, which the check would otherwise trip); skipping the step keeps this required
      # check green there.
      - name: Require a changeset for each changed publishable package
        if: ${{ !startsWith(github.head_ref, 'changeset-release/') }}
        env:
          CHANGESET_BASE: ${{ github.base_ref }}
        run: vp run release:coverage

  docs-and-internal-only:
    needs: detect-release-impact
    if: needs.detect-release-impact.outputs.release_impact != 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Skip changeset requirement
        run: |
          echo "No release-impacting files changed."
          echo "Changeset requirement is skipped for docs/internal-only PRs."

# Release/publish immutability posture — pantoken (thedannywahl/pantoken)

## PART A — Release/publish code

Files read: `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`. Sibling files in `scripts/release/` also present (changed-packages, check-changeset-coverage, workspace-packages, repository-metadata, sync/check-repository-metadata, seed-initial-package-changelogs) plus test files; the publish logic lives entirely in `publish-npm.ts` and the workflow.

### 1. Authentication + provenance
- **OIDC trusted publishing — no NPM_TOKEN.** Publishing uses npm CLI OIDC "trusted publishing." The workflow sets `permissions: id-token: write` (release.yml line 31) and `publishPackage()` runs `npm publish --provenance --access public` (publish-npm.ts lines 129-137) with no token. Requires a per-package trusted publisher configured on npmjs.com for repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow `release.yml`.
- **Provenance is ON, two ways:** `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` env at workflow level (release.yml line 133) AND the explicit `--provenance` flag on the publish command. So npm generates and attaches a provenance/SLSA attestation.
- **npmrc handling for OIDC:** the "Prepare npm for OIDC publishing" step (release.yml lines 82-87) strips any `_authToken` line from the npmrc via `sed -i '/_authToken/d'`. This is required because `setup-node`'s `registry-url` writes an empty `_authToken` entry that would otherwise force ENEEDAUTH instead of OIDC fallback.
- **Critical execution detail:** publish is invoked as plain `node scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` (release.yml line 120), NOT via the `vp run` launcher, because `vp run` scrubs the `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_*` env vars npm needs for the OIDC exchange.
- They deliberately avoid `changeset publish` (which shells to `pnpm publish`, whose OIDC exchange is broken per pnpm #9812/#11513).

### 2. Git tags + GitHub releases (`gh release create`)
- Tags and releases are created together by the GitHub API via `gh release create <tag> --repo <repo> --target <sha> --title <tag> --notes-file <notes>` in `ensureRelease()` (publish-npm.ts lines 185-196). The tag is created by this call (no separate `git tag`/`git push`). `createGithubReleases: false` is set on the changesets action so it does not also try (release.yml line 126).
- **Idempotent / non-overwriting.** Before creating, `ensureRelease()` calls `versionReleased()` and returns `"exists"` (skips) if a release already exists (lines 178-179). `versionReleased()` checks BOTH the current tag scheme `<name>@<version>` and the legacy `<name>@v<version>` (lines 159-161) via `gh release view`. So an existing release/tag is never re-created and there is **no `--clobber` or force flag** — existing release assets and tags are not overwritten. A re-run only backfills what's missing.
- **Overwrite risk assessment:** Low from this code path. There is no force-push of tags, no `gh release upload --clobber`, no `gh release delete`. Tag creation goes through `gh release create` which fails (non-fatally, logged and counted as `failed`) if the release already exists rather than overwriting. The target commit is `GITHUB_SHA` in CI, else local HEAD (lines 204-208).
- Tag naming: `tagFor()` = `${name}@${version}`, e.g. `@pantoken/css@0.2.0` (lines 69-72).

### 3. Provenance / attestations / SLSA / signing
- npm **provenance/attestations** are enabled (see #1) — this produces signed SLSA provenance attestations published to the npm registry via Sigstore, tied to the OIDC identity.
- **No separate artifact signing** (no cosign, no GPG tag signing, no SLSA generator action) beyond what `npm publish --provenance` provides.
- **No CodeQL/code-scanning** in the release path (confirmed off in Part B).

### 4. npm CLI version pinning
- **Not pinned.** The prepare step runs `npm install -g npm@latest` (release.yml line 84). The comment notes npm ≥ 11.5.1 is required for OIDC, but the workflow installs `@latest` rather than a pinned version, so the npm CLI version floats.
- Node is pinned to major `"22"` via setup-node (line 67), registry set to `https://registry.npmjs.org`.
- npmrc: no committed `.npmrc` with auth; the runner npmrc is generated by setup-node and then sanitized (see #1).

# Harden pantoken: protect main, immutable releases, supply-chain best practices

## Context

pantoken publishes many packages to npm. The release flow is automated (changesets → OIDC
trusted publishing with provenance) and just gained a branch ruleset requiring `ci-gate` /
`changeset-gate`. The audit found a solid base but real gaps: **0/12 GitHub Actions are
SHA-pinned** (mutable `@v1`/`@v7` tags, including three third-party actions — one running under
`contents:write` + `id-token:write` in the release job), **immutable releases is OFF**, **tags
are unprotected**, main protection is checks-only (no force-push/deletion block, no PR
requirement), and there's no Dependabot config, CodeQL, or least-privilege split in `docs.yml`.

Goal: lock down main, make releases tamper-proof (immutable + protected tags), and close the
supply-chain gaps — without ever deadlocking the solo-maintainer, bot-driven Version PR flow.

**Why the flow can't break (grounding facts, verified in code):**
- The changesets bot pushes `chore: version packages` to `changeset-release/main` and opens a PR;
  it never pushes to `main` directly. Main-scoped rules bite only at PR merge.
- `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` calls `gh release create <name>@<version>` — always a *new*
  unique tag/release, and `versionReleased()` skips ones that already exist. No tag moves, no
  deletes, no asset re-uploads, no release edits. So immutable releases + tag `non_fast_forward` +
  `deletion` never interfere.
- CI on the Version PR depends on `RELEASE_PAT` (already set); once we require PR + checks, that
  PAT is load-bearing — without it the PR's checks would park in `action_required` and deadlock.

**Confirmed choices:** squash-only merges · include CodeQL + harden-runner (audit) + required
signed commits · add repo admin (me) as a break-glass bypass actor on the main ruleset.

## Rollout order (each phase safe; nothing toggled mid-release)

Precondition: run while the release flow is at rest — main green, no open Version PR, no pending
files in `.changeset/`. Confirm `RELEASE_PAT` is present (`gh secret list`).

### Phase 1 — Repo settings (gh api, admin; no code)
1. Squash-only: `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken -X PATCH -F allow_merge_commit=false -F allow_rebase_merge=false -F allow_squash_merge=true`
2. Hygiene: same PATCH with `delete_branch_on_merge=true`, `allow_update_branch=true`
   (auto-deleting `changeset-release/main` is fine — the action recreates it; the main deletion
   block in Phase 5 targets `main` only).
3. Dependabot security updates: `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/automated-security-fixes -X PUT`
4. (Minor) enable secret-scanning validity checks + non-provider patterns via a
   `security_and_analysis` PATCH.

### Phase 2 — Non-blocking workflow/config hardening (ONE PR, dogfoods ci-gate/changeset-gate)
Files:
- **All 5 workflows** in `.github/workflows/` — SHA-pin every `uses:` to a full 40-hex commit SHA
  with a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment. Resolve each tag → SHA at execution via
  `gh api repos/<action-owner>/<action-repo>/commits/<tag> --jq .sha`. The 11 distinct actions:
  `actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-node@v7`, `actions/cache@v6` (+`/restore`),
  `actions/upload-artifact@v7`, `actions/download-artifact@v8`, `actions/configure-pages@v6`,
  `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5`, `actions/deploy-pages@v5`, and the three third-party
  (priority): `voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1`, `dorny/paths-filter@v4`, `changesets/action@v1`.
- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** (new) — `github-actions` (weekly, grouped, `ci:` prefix) + `npm`
  (weekly, dev-deps grouped, `chore:` prefix; reads `pnpm-lock.yaml`), `directory: "/"`. Keeps the
  SHAs and deps current so pinning doesn't rot.
- **`.github/workflows/docs.yml`** — remove top-level `id-token: write` + `pages: write`; grant
  them on the `deploy` job only (least privilege).
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — pin npm to a specific version ≥ 11.5.1 instead of
  `npm install -g npm@latest` (resolve current patch at execution).
- **`.github/workflows/changeset-check.yml`** + **`copilot-setup-steps.yml`** — add PR-scoped
  `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (latest run supplies the required-check status).
- **`.github/workflows/harden-runner.yml` steps** — add `step-security/harden-runner@<sha>` with
  `egress-policy: audit` as the first step of the `release` job (release.yml) and the `deploy` job
  (docs.yml). Non-blocking telemetry. (Also SHA-pinned.)
- **`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`** (new) — CodeQL for `javascript-typescript` on `pull_request`,
  `push: [main]`, and a weekly `schedule`. **Not** added to branch protection (must never gate
  releases). Actions in it SHA-pinned too.

Merge this PR through the existing gates; confirm a green CI run on main.

### Phase 3 — Tag protection ruleset (gh api)
`POST /repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/rulesets`:
```json
{ "name": "Protect all tags", "target": "tag", "enforcement": "active",
  "conditions": { "ref_name": { "include": ["~ALL"], "exclude": [] } },
  "rules": [ { "type": "deletion" }, { "type": "non_fast_forward" } ],
  "bypass_actors": [] }
```

### Phase 4 — Enable immutable releases (gh api)
`gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/immutable-releases -X PUT` (currently `{"enabled":false}`).
Optional confirm: `workflow_dispatch` the Release workflow — a fresh release must still cut (the
idempotent path skips existing ones; publish is unaffected).

### Phase 5 — Harden the main branch ruleset (gh api, two steps)
Update ruleset `19702834` (`main: require green checks before merge`). PUT the FULL `rules` array
so the existing checks aren't dropped, and add me as a break-glass bypass actor
(`bypass_actors: [{ "actor_id": <repo-admin-role-id>, "actor_type": "RepositoryRole", "bypass_mode": "always" }]`
— resolve the admin role id at execution).

Step 5a — add the never-interfering rules first: `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`.
Step 5b — add the `pull_request` rule (squash-only) + re-assert `required_status_checks`:
```json
"rules": [
  { "type": "deletion" },
  { "type": "non_fast_forward" },
  { "type": "pull_request", "parameters": {
      "required_approving_review_count": 0,
      "dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push": false,
      "require_code_owner_review": false,
      "require_last_push_approval": false,
      "required_review_thread_resolution": false,
      "automatic_copilot_code_review_enabled": false,
      "allowed_merge_methods": ["squash"] } },
  { "type": "required_status_checks", "parameters": {
      "strict_required_status_checks_policy": false,
      "do_not_enforce_on_create": false,
      "required_status_checks": [ { "context": "ci-gate" }, { "context": "changeset-gate" } ] } }
]
```
`required_approving_review_count: 0` avoids the solo self-approval deadlock while still forcing the
PR + checks flow. Validate with one throwaway feature PR via `--auto`.

### Phase 6 — Watch one real Version-PR cycle merge + publish end to end.

### Phase 7 — Required signed commits (last, after squash-only is proven)
Add `{ "type": "required_signatures" }` to the main ruleset `rules` array. Safe only because
merges are squash-only (GitHub re-signs the squashed commit; a merge/rebase would drag the
unsigned bot commit onto main and be rejected). Test by squash-merging the next Version PR.

## Key files
- `.github/workflows/{ci,changeset-check,docs,release,copilot-setup-steps}.yml` — SHA pins,
  perms, npm pin, concurrency, harden-runner
- `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` — new
- `.github/dependabot.yml` — new
- `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` — read-only reference; no change needed (already immutability-safe)

## Verification
- **Actions pinned:** `grep -rE "uses:.*@v[0-9]" .github/workflows/` returns nothing; every `uses:`
  ends in a 40-hex SHA + `# vX` comment.
- **Immutable releases ON:** `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/immutable-releases` → `enabled:true`.
- **Rulesets:** `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/rules/branches/main` shows deletion,
  non_fast_forward, pull_request (squash-only), required_status_checks, required_signatures; a tag
  ruleset with deletion + non_fast_forward exists.
- **Settings:** repo shows squash-only, delete_branch_on_merge/allow_update_branch true, automated
  security fixes enabled.
- **Flow intact:** a throwaway feature PR auto-merges only when green; one full Version PR cycle
  publishes and cuts immutable releases; CodeQL + harden-runner run but do NOT appear in required
  checks (`rules/branches/main` must not list them).
- **Dependabot:** config validates (Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot) and opens grouped
  PRs that pass the gates.

# Harden pantoken: protect main, immutable releases, supply-chain best practices

## Context

pantoken publishes many packages to npm. The release flow is automated (changesets → OIDC
trusted publishing with provenance) and just gained a branch ruleset requiring `ci-gate` /
`changeset-gate`. The audit found a solid base but real gaps: **0/12 GitHub Actions are
SHA-pinned** (mutable `@v1`/`@v7` tags, including three third-party actions — one running under
`contents:write` + `id-token:write` in the release job), **immutable releases is OFF**, **tags
are unprotected**, main protection is checks-only (no force-push/deletion block, no PR
requirement), and there's no Dependabot config, CodeQL, or least-privilege split in `docs.yml`.

Goal: lock down main, make releases tamper-proof (immutable + protected tags), and close the
supply-chain gaps — without ever deadlocking the solo-maintainer, bot-driven Version PR flow.

**Why the flow can't break (grounding facts, verified in code):**
- The changesets bot pushes `chore: version packages` to `changeset-release/main` and opens a PR;
  it never pushes to `main` directly. Main-scoped rules bite only at PR merge.
- `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` calls `gh release create <name>@<version>` — always a *new*
  unique tag/release, and `versionReleased()` skips ones that already exist. No tag moves, no
  deletes, no asset re-uploads, no release edits. So immutable releases + tag `non_fast_forward` +
  `deletion` never interfere.
- CI on the Version PR depends on `RELEASE_PAT` (already set); once we require PR + checks, that
  PAT is load-bearing — without it the PR's checks would park in `action_required` and deadlock.

**Confirmed choices:** squash-only merges · include CodeQL + harden-runner (audit) + required
signed commits · add repo admin (me) as a break-glass bypass actor on the main ruleset.

## Rollout order (each phase safe; nothing toggled mid-release)

Precondition: run while the release flow is at rest — main green, no open Version PR, no pending
files in `.changeset/`. Confirm `RELEASE_PAT` is present (`gh secret list`).

### Phase 1 — Repo settings (gh api, admin; no code)
1. Squash-only: `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken -X PATCH -F allow_merge_commit=false -F allow_rebase_merge=false -F allow_squash_merge=true`
2. Hygiene: same PATCH with `delete_branch_on_merge=true`, `allow_update_branch=true`
   (auto-deleting `changeset-release/main` is fine — the action recreates it; the main deletion
   block in Phase 5 targets `main` only).
3. Dependabot security updates: `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/automated-security-fixes -X PUT`
4. (Minor) enable secret-scanning validity checks + non-provider patterns via a
   `security_and_analysis` PATCH.

### Phase 2 — Non-blocking workflow/config hardening (ONE PR, dogfoods ci-gate/changeset-gate)
Files:
- **All 5 workflows** in `.github/workflows/` — SHA-pin every `uses:` to a full 40-hex commit SHA
  with a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment. Resolve each tag → SHA at execution via
  `gh api repos/<action-owner>/<action-repo>/commits/<tag> --jq .sha`. The 11 distinct actions:
  `actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-node@v7`, `actions/cache@v6` (+`/restore`),
  `actions/upload-artifact@v7`, `actions/download-artifact@v8`, `actions/configure-pages@v6`,
  `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5`, `actions/deploy-pages@v5`, and the three third-party
  (priority): `voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1`, `dorny/paths-filter@v4`, `changesets/action@v1`.
- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** (new) — `github-actions` (weekly, grouped, `ci:` prefix) + `npm`
  (weekly, dev-deps grouped, `chore:` prefix; reads `pnpm-lock.yaml`), `directory: "/"`. Keeps the
  SHAs and deps current so pinning doesn't rot.
- **`.github/workflows/docs.yml`** — remove top-level `id-token: write` + `pages: write`; grant
  them on the `deploy` job only (least privilege).
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — pin npm to a specific version ≥ 11.5.1 instead of
  `npm install -g npm@latest` (resolve current patch at execution).
- **`.github/workflows/changeset-check.yml`** + **`copilot-setup-steps.yml`** — add PR-scoped
  `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (latest run supplies the required-check status).

  `egress-policy: audit` as the first step of the `release` job (release.yml) and the `deploy` job
  (docs.yml). Non-blocking telemetry. (Also SHA-pinned.)
- **`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`** (new) — CodeQL for `javascript-typescript` on `pull_request`,
  `push: [main]`, and a weekly `schedule`. **Not** added to branch protection (must never gate
  releases). Actions in it SHA-pinned too.

### Phase 3 — Tag protection ruleset (gh api)
`POST /repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/rulesets`:
```json

  "conditions": { "ref_name": { "include": ["~ALL"], "exclude": [] } },
  "rules": [ { "type": "deletion" }, { "type": "non_fast_forward" } ],
  "bypass_actors": [] }
```

input.plan:
# Harden pantoken: protect main, immutable releases, supply-chain best practices

## Context

pantoken publishes many packages to npm. The release flow is automated (changesets → OIDC
trusted publishing with provenance) and just gained a branch ruleset requiring `ci-gate` /
`changeset-gate`. The audit found a solid base but real gaps: **0/12 GitHub Actions are
SHA-pinned** (mutable `@v1`/`@v7` tags, including three third-party actions — one running under
`contents:write` + `id-token:write` in the release job), **immutable releases is OFF**, **tags
are unprotected**, main protection is checks-only (no force-push/deletion block, no PR
requirement), and there's no Dependabot config, CodeQL, or least-privilege split in `docs.yml`.

Goal: lock down main, make releases tamper-proof (immutable + protected tags), and close the
supply-chain gaps — without ever deadlocking the solo-maintainer, bot-driven Version PR flow.

**Why the flow can't break (grounding facts, verified in code):**
- The changesets bot pushes `chore: version packages` to `changeset-release/main` and opens a PR;
  it never pushes to `main` directly. Main-scoped rules bite only at PR merge.
- `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` calls `gh release create <name>@<version>` — always a *new*
  unique tag/release, and `versionReleased()` skips ones that already exist. No tag moves, no
  deletes, no asset re-uploads, no release edits. So immutable releases + tag `non_fast_forward` +
  `deletion` never interfere.
- CI on the Version PR depends on `RELEASE_PAT` (already set); once we require PR + checks, that
  PAT is load-bearing — without it the PR's checks would park in `action_required` and deadlock.

**Confirmed choices:** squash-only merges · include CodeQL + harden-runner (audit) + required
signed commits · add repo admin (me) as a break-glass bypass actor on the main ruleset.

## Rollout order (each phase safe; nothing toggled mid-release)

Precondition: run while the release flow is at rest — main green, no open Version PR, no pending
files in `.changeset/`. Confirm `RELEASE_PAT` is present (`gh secret list`).

### Phase 1 — Repo settings (gh api, admin; no code)
1. Squash-only: `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken -X PATCH -F allow_merge_commit=false -F allow_rebase_merge=false -F allow_squash_merge=true`
2. Hygiene: same PATCH with `delete_branch_on_merge=true`, `allow_update_branch=true`
   (auto-deleting `changeset-release/main` is fine — the action recreates it; the main deletion
   block in Phase 5 targets `main` only).
3. Dependabot security updates: `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/automated-security-fixes -X PUT`
4. (Minor) enable secret-scanning validity checks + non-provider patterns via a
   `security_and_analysis` PATCH.

### Phase 2 — Non-blocking workflow/config hardening (ONE PR, dogfoods ci-gate/changeset-gate)
Files:
- **All 5 workflows** in `.github/workflows/` — SHA-pin every `uses:` to a full 40-hex commit SHA
  with a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment. Resolve each tag → SHA at execution via
  `gh api repos/<action-owner>/<action-repo>/commits/<tag> --jq .sha`. The 11 distinct actions:
  `actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-node@v7`, `actions/cache@v6` (+`/restore`),
  `actions/upload-artifact@v7`, `actions/download-artifact@v8`, `actions/configure-pages@v6`,
  `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5`, `actions/deploy-pages@v5`, and the three third-party
  (priority): `voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1`, `dorny/paths-filter@v4`, `changesets/action@v1`.
- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** (new) — `github-actions` (weekly, grouped, `ci:` prefix) + `npm`
  (weekly, dev-deps grouped, `chore:` prefix; reads `pnpm-lock.yaml`), `directory: "/"`. Keeps the
  SHAs and deps current so pinning doesn't rot.
- **`.github/workflows/docs.yml`** — remove top-level `id-token: write` + `pages: write`; grant
  them on the `deploy` job only (least privilege).
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — pin npm to a specific version ≥ 11.5.1 instead of
  `npm install -g npm@latest` (resolve current patch at execution).
- **`.github/workflows/changeset-check.yml`** + **`copilot-setup-steps.yml`** — add PR-scoped
  `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (latest run supplies the required-check status).
- **`.github/workflows/harden-runner.yml` steps** — add `step-security/harden-runner@<sha>` with
  `egress-policy: audit` as the first step of the `release` job (release.yml) and the `deploy` job
  (docs.yml). Non-blocking telemetry. (Also SHA-pinned.)
- **`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`** (new) — CodeQL for `javascript-typescript` on `pull_request`,
  `push: [main]`, and a weekly `schedule`. **Not** added to branch protection (must never gate
  releases). Actions in it SHA-pinned too.

Merge this PR through the existing gates; confirm a green CI run on main.

### Phase 3 — Tag protection ruleset (gh api)
`POST /repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/rulesets`:
```json
{ "name": "Protect all tags", "target": "tag", "enforcement": "active",
  "conditions": { "ref_name": { "include": ["~ALL"], "exclude": [] } },
  "rules": [ { "type": "deletion" }, { "type": "non_fast_forward" } ],
  "bypass_actors": [] }
```

### Phase 4 — Enable immutable releases (gh api)
`gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/immutable-releases -X PUT` (currently `{"enabled":false}`).
Optional confirm: `workflow_dispatch` the Release workflow — a fresh release must still cut (the
idempotent path skips existing ones; publish is unaffected).

### Phase 5 — Harden the main branch ruleset (gh api, two steps)
Update ruleset `19702834` (`main: require green checks before merge`). PUT the FULL `rules` array
so the existing checks aren't dropped, and add me as a break-glass bypass actor
(`bypass_actors: [{ "actor_id": <repo-admin-role-id>, "actor_type": "RepositoryRole", "bypass_mode": "always" }]`
— resolve the admin role id at execution).

Step 5a — add the never-interfering rules first: `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`.
Step 5b — add the `pull_request` rule (squash-only) + re-assert `required_status_checks`:
```json
"rules": [
  { "type": "deletion" },
  { "type": "non_fast_forward" },
  { "type": "pull_request", "parameters": {
      "required_approving_review_count": 0,
      "dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push": false,
      "require_code_owner_review": false,
      "require_last_push_approval": false,
      "required_review_thread_resolution": false,
      "automatic_copilot_code_review_enabled": false,
      "allowed_merge_methods": ["squash"] } },
  { "type": "required_status_checks", "parameters": {
      "strict_required_status_checks_policy": false,
      "do_not_enforce_on_create": false,
      "required_status_checks": [ { "context": "ci-gate" }, { "context": "changeset-gate" } ] } }
]
```
`required_approving_review_count: 0` avoids the solo self-approval deadlock while still forcing the
PR + checks flow. Validate with one throwaway feature PR via `--auto`.

### Phase 6 — Watch one real Version-PR cycle merge + publish end to end.

### Phase 7 — Required signed commits (last, after squash-only is proven)
Add `{ "type": "required_signatures" }` to the main ruleset `rules` array. Safe only because
merges are squash-only (GitHub re-signs the squashed commit; a merge/rebase would drag the
unsigned bot commit onto main and be rejected). Test by squash-merging the next Version PR.

## Key files
- `.github/workflows/{ci,changeset-check,docs,release,copilot-setup-steps}.yml` — SHA pins,
  perms, npm pin, concurrency, harden-runner
- `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` — new
- `.github/dependabot.yml` — new
- `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` — read-only reference; no change needed (already immutability-safe)

## Verification
- **Actions pinned:** `grep -rE "uses:.*@v[0-9]" .github/workflows/` returns nothing; every `uses:`
  ends in a 40-hex SHA + `# vX` comment.
- **Immutable releases ON:** `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/immutable-releases` → `enabled:true`.
- **Rulesets:** `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/rules/branches/main` shows deletion,
  non_fast_forward, pull_request (squash-only), required_status_checks, required_signatures; a tag
  ruleset with deletion + non_fast_forward exists.
- **Settings:** repo shows squash-only, delete_branch_on_merge/allow_update_branch true, automated
  security fixes enabled.
- **Flow intact:** a throwaway feature PR auto-merges only when green; one full Version PR cycle
  publishes and cuts immutable releases; CodeQL + harden-runner run but do NOT appear in required
  checks (`rules/branches/main` must not list them).
- **Dependabot:** config validates (Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot) and opens grouped
  PRs that pass the gates.

# Harden pantoken: protect main, immutable releases, supply-chain best practices

## Context

pantoken publishes many packages to npm. The release flow is automated (changesets → OIDC
trusted publishing with provenance) and just gained a branch ruleset requiring `ci-gate` /
`changeset-gate`. The audit found a solid base but real gaps: **0/12 GitHub Actions are
SHA-pinned** (mutable `@v1`/`@v7` tags, including three third-party actions — one running under
`contents:write` + `id-token:write` in the release job), **immutable releases is OFF**, **tags
are unprotected**, main protection is checks-only (no force-push/deletion block, no PR
requirement), and there's no Dependabot config, CodeQL, or least-privilege split in `docs.yml`.

Goal: lock down main, make releases tamper-proof (immutable + protected tags), and close the
supply-chain gaps — without ever deadlocking the solo-maintainer, bot-driven Version PR flow.

**Why the flow can't break (grounding facts, verified in code):**
- The changesets bot pushes `chore: version packages` to `changeset-release/main` and opens a PR;
  it never pushes to `main` directly. Main-scoped rules bite only at PR merge.
- `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` calls `gh release create <name>@<version>` — always a *new*
  unique tag/release, and `versionReleased()` skips ones that already exist. No tag moves, no
  deletes, no asset re-uploads, no release edits. So immutable releases + tag `non_fast_forward` +
  `deletion` never interfere.
- CI on the Version PR depends on `RELEASE_PAT` (already set); once we require PR + checks, that
  PAT is load-bearing — without it the PR's checks would park in `action_required` and deadlock.

**Confirmed choices:** squash-only merges · include CodeQL + harden-runner (audit) + required
signed commits · add repo admin (me) as a break-glass bypass actor on the main ruleset.

## Rollout order (each phase safe; nothing toggled mid-release)

Precondition: run while the release flow is at rest — main green, no open Version PR, no pending
files in `.changeset/`. Confirm `RELEASE_PAT` is present (`gh secret list`).

### Phase 1 — Repo settings (gh api, admin; no code)
1. Squash-only: `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken -X PATCH -F allow_merge_commit=false -F allow_rebase_merge=false -F allow_squash_merge=true`
2. Hygiene: same PATCH with `delete_branch_on_merge=true`, `allow_update_branch=true`
   (auto-deleting `changeset-release/main` is fine — the action recreates it; the main deletion
   block in Phase 5 targets `main` only).
3. Dependabot security updates: `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/automated-security-fixes -X PUT`
4. (Minor) enable secret-scanning validity checks + non-provider patterns via a
   `security_and_analysis` PATCH.

### Phase 2 — Non-blocking workflow/config hardening (ONE PR, dogfoods ci-gate/changeset-gate)
Files:
- **All 5 workflows** in `.github/workflows/` — SHA-pin every `uses:` to a full 40-hex commit SHA
  with a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment. Resolve each tag → SHA at execution via
  `gh api repos/<action-owner>/<action-repo>/commits/<tag> --jq .sha`. The 11 distinct actions:
  `actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-node@v7`, `actions/cache@v6` (+`/restore`),
  `actions/upload-artifact@v7`, `actions/download-artifact@v8`, `actions/configure-pages@v6`,
  `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5`, `actions/deploy-pages@v5`, and the three third-party
  (priority): `voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1`, `dorny/paths-filter@v4`, `changesets/action@v1`.
- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** (new) — `github-actions` (weekly, grouped, `ci:` prefix) + `npm`
  (weekly, dev-deps grouped, `chore:` prefix; reads `pnpm-lock.yaml`), `directory: "/"`. Keeps the
  SHAs and deps current so pinning doesn't rot.
- **`.github/workflows/docs.yml`** — remove top-level `id-token: write` + `pages: write`; grant
  them on the `deploy` job only (least privilege).
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — pin npm to a specific version ≥ 11.5.1 instead of
  `npm install -g npm@latest` (resolve current patch at execution).
- **`.github/workflows/changeset-check.yml`** + **`copilot-setup-steps.yml`** — add PR-scoped
  `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (latest run supplies the required-check status).
- **`.github/workflows/harden-runner.yml` steps** — add `step-security/harden-runner@<sha>` with
  `egress-policy: audit` as the first step of the `release` job (release.yml) and the `deploy` job
  (docs.yml). Non-blocking telemetry. (Also SHA-pinned.)
- **`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`** (new) — CodeQL for `javascript-typescript` on `pull_request`,
  `push: [main]`, and a weekly `schedule`. **Not** added to branch protection (must never gate
  releases). Actions in it SHA-pinned too.

Merge this PR through the existing gates; confirm a green CI run on main.

### Phase 3 — Tag protection ruleset (gh api)
`POST /repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/rulesets`:
```json
{ "name": "Protect all tags", "target": "tag", "enforcement": "active",
  "conditions": { "ref_name": { "include": ["~ALL"], "exclude": [] } },
  "rules": [ { "type": "deletion" }, { "type": "non_fast_forward" } ],
  "bypass_actors": [] }
```

### Phase 4 — Enable immutable releases (gh api)
`gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/immutable-releases -X PUT` (currently `{"enabled":false}`).
Optional confirm: `workflow_dispatch` the Release workflow — a fresh release must still cut (the
idempotent path skips existing ones; publish is unaffected).

### Phase 5 — Harden the main branch ruleset (gh api, two steps)
Update ruleset `19702834` (`main: require green checks before merge`). PUT the FULL `rules` array
so the existing checks aren't dropped, and add me as a break-glass bypass actor
(`bypass_actors: [{ "actor_id": <repo-admin-role-id>, "actor_type": "RepositoryRole", "bypass_mode": "always" }]`
— resolve the admin role id at execution).

Step 5a — add the never-interfering rules first: `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`.
Step 5b — add the `pull_request` rule (squash-only) + re-assert `required_status_checks`:
```json
"rules": [
  { "type": "deletion" },
  { "type": "non_fast_forward" },
  { "type": "pull_request", "parameters": {
      "required_approving_review_count": 0,
      "dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push": false,
      "require_code_owner_review": false,
      "require_last_push_approval": false,
      "required_review_thread_resolution": false,
      "automatic_copilot_code_review_enabled": false,
      "allowed_merge_methods": ["squash"] } },
  { "type": "required_status_checks", "parameters": {
      "strict_required_status_checks_policy": false,
      "do_not_enforce_on_create": false,
      "required_status_checks": [ { "context": "ci-gate" }, { "context": "changeset-gate" } ] } }
]
```
`required_approving_review_count: 0` avoids the solo self-approval deadlock while still forcing the
PR + checks flow. Validate with one throwaway feature PR via `--auto`.

### Phase 6 — Watch one real Version-PR cycle merge + publish end to end.

### Phase 7 — Required signed commits (last, after squash-only is proven)
Add `{ "type": "required_signatures" }` to the main ruleset `rules` array. Safe only because
merges are squash-only (GitHub re-signs the squashed commit; a merge/rebase would drag the
unsigned bot commit onto main and be rejected). Test by squash-merging the next Version PR.

## Key files
- `.github/workflows/{ci,changeset-check,docs,release,copilot-setup-steps}.yml` — SHA pins,
  perms, npm pin, concurrency, harden-runner
- `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` — new
- `.github/dependabot.yml` — new
- `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` — read-only reference; no change needed (already immutability-safe)

## Verification
- **Actions pinned:** `grep -rE "uses:.*@v[0-9]" .github/workflows/` returns nothing; every `uses:`
  ends in a 40-hex SHA + `# vX` comment.
- **Immutable releases ON:** `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/immutable-releases` → `enabled:true`.
- **Rulesets:** `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/rules/branches/main` shows deletion,
  non_fast_forward, pull_request (squash-only), required_status_checks, required_signatures; a tag
  ruleset with deletion + non_fast_forward exists.
- **Settings:** repo shows squash-only, delete_branch_on_merge/allow_update_branch true, automated
  security fixes enabled.
- **Flow intact:** a throwaway feature PR auto-merges only when green; one full Version PR cycle
  publishes and cuts immutable releases; CodeQL + harden-runner run but do NOT appear in required
  checks (`rules/branches/main` must not list them).
- **Dependabot:** config validates (Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot) and opens grouped
  PRs that pass the gates.

  PAT is load-bearing — without it the PR's checks would park in `action_required` and deadlock.

**Confirmed choices:** squash-only merges · harden-runner (audit) + required signed commits · add

**Out of scope here (in-flight on another worktree):** SHA-pinning all GitHub Actions,

   block in Phase 5 targets `main` only).
3. Dependabot security updates: `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/automated-security-fixes -X PUT`
4. (Minor) enable secret-scanning validity checks + non-provider patterns via a

- **All 5 workflows** in `.github/workflows/` — SHA-pin every `uses:` to a full 40-hex commit SHA
  with a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment. Resolve each tag → SHA at execution via
  `gh api repos/<action-owner>/<action-repo>/commits/<tag> --jq .sha`. The 11 distinct actions:
  `actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-node@v7`, `actions/cache@v6` (+`/restore`),
  `actions/upload-artifact@v7`, `actions/download-artifact@v8`, `actions/configure-pages@v6`,
  `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5`, `actions/deploy-pages@v5`, and the three third-party
  (priority): `voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1`, `dorny/paths-filter@v4`, `changesets/action@v1`.
- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** (new) — `github-actions` (weekly, grouped, `ci:` prefix) + `npm`
  (weekly, dev-deps grouped, `chore:` prefix; reads `pnpm-lock.yaml`), `directory: "/"`. Keeps the
  SHAs and deps current so pinning doesn't rot.
- **`.github/workflows/docs.yml`** — remove top-level `id-token: write` + `pages: write`; grant
  them on the `deploy` job only (least privilege).
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — pin npm to a specific version ≥ 11.5.1 instead of
  `npm install -g npm@latest` (resolve current patch at execution).
- **`.github/workflows/changeset-check.yml`** + **`copilot-setup-steps.yml`** — add PR-scoped
  `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (latest run supplies the required-check status).
- **`.github/workflows/harden-runner.yml` steps** — add `step-security/harden-runner@<sha>` with
  `egress-policy: audit` as the first step of the `release` job (release.yml) and the `deploy` job
  (docs.yml). Non-blocking telemetry. (Also SHA-pinned.)
- **`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`** (new) — CodeQL for `javascript-typescript` on `pull_request`,
  `push: [main]`, and a weekly `schedule`. **Not** added to branch protection (must never gate
  releases). Actions in it SHA-pinned too.

`POST /repos/thedannywahl/pantoken/rulesets`:
```json

  "rules": [ { "type": "deletion" }, { "type": "non_fast_forward" } ],

```

idempotent path skips existing ones; publish is unaffected).

### Phase 5 — Harden the main branch ruleset (gh api, two steps)

so the existing checks aren't dropped, and add me as a break-glass bypass actor

— resolve the admin role id at execution).

```json
  { "type": "non_fast_forward" },
  { "type": "pull_request", "parameters": {

      "dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push": false,
      "require_code_owner_review": false,
      "require_last_push_approval": false,
      "required_review_thread_resolution": false,
      "automatic_copilot_code_review_enabled": false,

      "do_not_enforce_on_create": false,
      "required_status_checks": [ { "context": "ci-gate" }, { "context": "changeset-gate" } ] } }
```

# Harden pantoken: protect main, immutable releases, supply-chain best practices

## Context

pantoken publishes many packages to npm. The release flow is automated (changesets → OIDC
trusted publishing with provenance) and just gained a branch ruleset requiring `ci-gate` /
`changeset-gate`. The audit found a solid base but real gaps: **0/12 GitHub Actions are
SHA-pinned** (mutable `@v1`/`@v7` tags, including three third-party actions — one running under

requirement), and there's no Dependabot config, CodeQL, or least-privilege split in `docs.yml`.

- `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` calls `gh release create <name>@<version>` — always a *new*

  deletes, no asset re-uploads, no release edits. So immutable releases + tag `non_fast_forward` +

## Context

pantoken publishes many packages to npm. The release flow is automated (changesets → OIDC
trusted publishing with provenance) and just gained a branch ruleset requiring `ci-gate` /
`changeset-gate`. The audit found a solid base but real gaps: **0/12 GitHub Actions are
SHA-pinned** (mutable `@v1`/`@v7` tags, including three third-party actions — one running under
`contents:write` + `id-token:write` in the release job), **immutable releases is OFF**, **tags
are unprotected**, main protection is checks-only (no force-push/deletion block, no PR
requirement), and there's no Dependabot config, CodeQL, or least-privilege split in `docs.yml`.

Goal: lock down main, make releases tamper-proof (immutable + protected tags), and close the
supply-chain gaps — without ever deadlocking the solo-maintainer, bot-driven Version PR flow.

**Why the flow can't break (grounding facts, verified in code):**
- The changesets bot pushes `chore: version packages` to `changeset-release/main` and opens a PR;
  it never pushes to `main` directly. Main-scoped rules bite only at PR merge.
- `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` calls `gh release create <name>@<version>` — always a *new*
  unique tag/release, and `versionReleased()` skips ones that already exist. No tag moves, no
  deletes, no asset re-uploads, no release edits. So immutable releases + tag `non_fast_forward` +
  `deletion` never interfere.
- CI on the Version PR depends on `RELEASE_PAT` (already set); once we require PR + checks, that
  PAT is load-bearing — without it the PR's checks would park in `action_required` and deadlock.

**Confirmed choices:** squash-only merges · harden-runner (audit) + required signed commits · add
